name: com.unity.burst
description: Burst is a compiler that translates from IL/.NET bytecode to highly optimized native code using LLVM.

_upm.changelog:
### Fixed
- Fix error while verifying module from invalid bitcast when converting nunit to float or double.
- Fixed cases where the Burst Inspector could jitter when moving the divider.
- Fixed that using a Bursted function pointer as argument to a method directly could cause a compiler error
- Fixed Burst AOT builds for Embedded Linux and QNX when using Build Profiles: Burst now reads the active profile’s architecture instead of a stale editor setting, preventing sysroot/linker failures (e.g. x64 SDK with aarch64 target) in batchmode and CI.
- Atomics were not generated when target web platform with threading enabled.
- Fixed a race between Burst and the Editor compilation pipeline that could surface as a `Failed to find entry-points` error.
- Burst could crash if Very Large static readonly data happened to be compiled in such a way that it would result in a direct store of the array. Now, the very large data is memmoved instead.
- Web Player would crash if targeting wasm and the entities package is present.
- Very large constants could cause Burst to crash when compiling for WebAssembly

### Changed
- Changed the default LLVM version to 21.
- The minimum required Linux version to use Burst in the Unity Editor is now Ubuntu 18.04 or equivalent.
- Changed minimum Editor version to 6.0
- `[IgnoreWarning(1371)]` applied to a `[BurstDiscard]` method now suppresses the discarded-call warning for the calls discarded along with it, instead of having to annotate every caller.

### Removed
- Removed support for LLVM 10, 15, 16, 17.

### Known Issues
- Windows Smart App Control or WDAC policies may block JIT-compiled libraries at load time. Burst now logs a warning in such cases and deletes the affected library, which will be recompiled so Burst can attempt loading it again.

### Added
- Support for Wasm64 target
- Added `ButtonFlowNewLineTest` editor test to verify that the Burst Inspector button bar wraps to a new line when the window is narrow, and fits on a single line when the window is wide.
- Added a Restart Now button to the dialog shown when the Burst package is removed or updated.
